card.name: The word chap in book citations
card.fires_on: The word "chap" (chapter) right after a textbook publisher and year in reference lists, such as "Saunders Elsevier; 2011:". Weaker hits occur on name endings in author credits and on "provider" in "health care provider".

modes.label: Chapter in citation
modes.description: The abbreviation "chap" after the year and colon in a textbook reference.
modes.example: Textbook of Endocrinology . 12th ed. Philadelphia, PA: Elsevier Saunders; 2011:<<chap>> 34. Jensen RT,

modes.label: Author name endings
modes.description: The last piece of a doctor's surname in the reviewer credit lines.
modes.example: 24th ed. Philadelphia, PA: Saunders Elsevier; 2011:chap 197. David C. Dug<<dale>>, III, MD, Professor of Medicine

modes.label: Health care provider
modes.description: The word "provider" in the phrase "call your health care provider".
modes.example: Call your health care<< provider>> if you develop any symptoms of insulinoma

card.plain: It fires on the "chap" in textbook chapter citations at the end of patient-information pages.
